point.note: B misses: a spell row and two rows with no figure; the structured-quantity shortcut over-fires.

band.note: A misses were rank names such as a range of ranks, now stripped.

order.note: Misses were 'rather than', 'superior' as a job title and 'later than' as a deadline; excluded after sampling (fix not re-sampled). B has only 3 rows.

count_or_duration.note: Misses were counts of steps or crowd sizes, not tries or days.

sequence.note: Broad kind: any rule with 3 or more listed steps counts. B misses were 'before the whole school' and 'after dark' used as time words.

tolerance.note: Poor. Most hits were 'within', 'correct' or 'wrong'; those words were removed after sampling (fix not re-sampled). Treat tolerance counts as unreliable.

negative.note: Misses were place names such as the forbidden corridor and 'lost' meaning wandering.

adjustment: One round of regex changes after the first sample (rank-number scrub for band, comparison words trimmed for order, tolerance narrowed, sequence trimmed to before/after/then, negative trimmed). Order, tolerance and sequence precision above is from the re-sample; point and count are from the first sample, whose regexes did not change. Two small last fixes (rather than, and the tolerance words) were applied without a re-sample.
changes: Almost every system with a price, wage, time or count in its rows clears the three-anchor bar, because the bar is low and the row sets are large. The class column says anchors exist, not that they are enough to fit a curve. A fit should count anchors per quantity it actually tunes.
Tolerance anchors are the thinnest kind in both books. Shapes such as 'too much fails' mostly sit in qualitative prose and need a targeted read before a fit relies on them.
Rows are the rule and rule-note passes only. Systems fed mainly by scenes or people rows (for example daily life) are undercounted here.
